newsitem.title: USA: Tosco to restart Pennsylvania refinery in April.
newsitem.headline: Tosco to restart Pennsylvania refinery in April.

text.p: Tosco Corp will restart the revamped Trainer, Penn., refinery in April, three months earlier than planned, according to the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers union.
The company will restart the refinery, which was shuttered about one year ago by British Petroleum before its sale to Tosco.
The refinery will probably operate with a 180,000 to 190,000 barrel per day (bpd) capacity, according to Dennis Stephano, president of the OCAW Local 8-234.
Tosco had previously said it would operate the refinery at about 150,000 bpd. Company officials were not immediately available to comment on the refinery.

Tosco took title to the plant last February, after acquiring the refinery for $25 million, and said it would spend another $50 million to upgrade, cutting the capacity from 180,000 bpd to concentrate on higher value light-end products.
"They'll probably try to run it full out. They didn't buy this plant to let it sit idle," Stephano said.
BP mothballed the plant before transferring the title to Tosco, after Tosco and OCAW failed to agree on staff reductions and on ending longstanding union work rules.
Tosco began the upgrades after reaching agreement with the Union to trim staff at the facility.
Tosco also paid also purchased the rights to sell its gasoline under the well-known BP name at about 500 gasoline stations on the East Coast.
